commit_message:
[Codegen] Fix ND vector elementwise unroll operands (#24458)

This crashed when compiling a proprietary model.

Unroll elementwise ops by grouping converted operands per result lane
and reuse single-value operand lists across all lanes. This handles
cases like scalar select predicates while keeping split vector operands
paired with their converted result lanes via zip_equal.

Add coverage for scalar and vector arith.select predicates, a 3-D
scalar-predicate select, and arith.cmpi so non-select elementwise ops
with different operand/result element types stay covered.

commit_message:
[Codegen] Preemptively duplicate operations before tile-size analysis (#24431)

To avoid cross-pollution from easy-to-duplicate operations such as
`linalg.fill` in tile size analysis, we treat them as duplicatable. So
far, the materialization of the vector tile size analysis duplicated
values on demand, based on the analysis result.

This approach has two main downsides: 
- The analysis code needs to account for duplicatable operations with
special logic. This logic started to become more complicated when I
tried to fix an issue with region control flow locally.
- It can be difficult to trace from the duplicatable operation to the
operation that actually uses that value with a specific tile size in the
presence of control-flow as pointed out
[here](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24246#discussion_r3187746878).
Locally handling `scf.for` introduced even more complexity.

Therefore, I decided to change the duplication to eager duplication:
Before the analysis, every duplicatable operation is duplicated for each
of its uses. Analysis can then run without special logic for
duplicatable values. Afterwards, operations are deduplicated as much as
possible again. Operations that are duplicates of the same original
value and have the same tile size will be deduplicated to a single
operation.

This approach avoids both downsides described above. The cost for the
increased IR size is completely local to the pass itself.

This contributes towards https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24221.

`linalg.fill` in tile size analysis, we treat them as duplicatable. So
far, the materialization of the vector tile size analysis duplicated
values on demand, based on the analysis result.

This approach has two main downsides: 
- The analysis code needs to account for duplicatable operations with
special logic. This logic started to become more complicated when I
tried to fix an issue with region control flow locally.
- It can be difficult to trace from the duplicatable operation to the
operation that actually uses that value with a specific tile size in the
presence of control-flow as pointed out
[here](https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24246#discussion_r3187746878).
Locally handling `scf.for` introduced even more complexity.

Therefore, I decided to change the duplication to eager duplication:
Before the analysis, every duplicatable operation is duplicated for each
of its uses. Analysis can then run without special logic for
duplicatable values. Afterwards, operations are deduplicated as much as
possible again. Operations that are duplicates of the same original
value and have the same tile size will be deduplicated to a single
operation.

This approach avoids both downsides described above. The cost for the
increased IR size is completely local to the pass itself.

This contributes towards https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24221.

commit_message:
[VectorDistribute] Distribute `vector.scan` to threads (#24312)

Implementation of vector distribution of `vector.scan` to threads.
Currently limited to threads in a single wave/subgroup, distribution
across subgroups in a workgroup will come as a follow-up PR to ease
review.

In contrast to reduction operations which produce a uniform result,
scans have one result per input element plus a second result for the
overall outcome. Therefore, the distribution is different from e.g.
`multi_reduction`.

This PR builds on top of the `subgroup_scan` operation introduced in
https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/24188. More details on the
algorithm can be found in the pattern documentation.

This is part of https://github.com/iree-org/iree/issues/24186.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Attach swizzle to inner_tiled encoder info. (#24455)

Follow-up to #24437. That commit made `getUndistributedTileTypes` honor
the swizzle's permutation, but the encoder side
(`getInnerTiledEncodingInfo`) was still producing a rank-2 row-major
inner tile that ignored the swizzle's `expand_shape` and permutation.
For existing intrinsics the two sides happen to be compatible under
`matchTileTypes`' unit-dim filter, but the encoder's rank-2 shape
disagrees with the rank-N permutation-aware tile type as soon as any
swizzle has a non-identity permutation (e.g. pre-transposed intrinsics,
added in a follow-up).

Set `info.swizzle = IREE::CPU::getSwizzle(mma, operandIdx)` so the pack
pipeline's existing `getSwizzledShape` bridge applies the swizzle's
`expand_shape` + `transpose` to the packed inner tile, matching the tile
type `getUndistributedTileTypes` returns. Mirrors GPU's
`getEncodingInfoImpl`. Drop the stale "Only used on GPU" comment on the
`swizzle` field.

Test fallout: `materialize_encoding_x86_64.mlir`'s four
`_inner_tiled_avx512` CHECK groups now expect the
`tensor.expand_shape` after each pack and the
`tensor.collapse_shape` before the unpack, with the rank-N inner tile
that the swizzle materializes.

Progress towards #24323.

commit_message:
[Codegen][AMDGPU] Teach prefetch pass to recognize global_transpose_load as read root (#24457)

Part of #24454.

`ROCDLPrefetchSharedMemoryCopy` performs software pipelining
of loops that stream data from global memory to shared memory. It
previously only
recognized `vector.transfer_read` as a global memory read root.

This PR extends the pass to also treat `amdgpu::GlobalTransposeLoadOp`
as a read
root, so that loops using `global_load_tr` for transpose loads get
pipelined the
same way.

commit_message:
[Codegen][CPU] Replace transposed_intrinsic with explicit pre-transposed enums. (#24456)

This is take two of #24404, which was reverted due to a RDNA4 regression
(#24427); see the regression delta at the end.

Each non-square hardware MMA now appears as two `MMAIntrinsic` enum
values — one per orientation — named after their actual MxNxK shape
(e.g. `MMA_X86_AVX512_1x16x1_F32_F32` and its M↔N-swapped sibling
`MMA_X86_AVX512_16x1x1_F32_F32`). The swapped sibling of `X` is `X | 1`
(bit 0 of D in the enum's encoding), so consecutive enum values form
natural/swapped pairs. The `transposed_intrinsic` boolean on
`DataTiledMMAAttr` is removed; both orientations show up as distinct
candidates in `getMmaIntrinsicsForTargetConfig` and the existing
`chooseIntrinsic` scoring picks between them.

A new `assert(isMmaIntrinsicArrayValid(...))` at the bottom of
`getMmaIntrinsicsForTargetConfig` enforces the convention: strictly
increasing, every swapped entry preceded by its natural sibling, and
square/type-symmetric singletons allowed (covers the generic-scalar
1×1×1 family).

Motivation: the boolean was originally there to avoid 2× enum growth,
but it leaked orientation-handling into every layer that touched MMA
layouts — swizzles, ACC encoding-info, the cross-intrinsic ACC index,
broadcast direction. It was also poised to get worse: asymmetric LLVM
intrinsics (vpdpbusd) and non-x86 targets (no broadcast) would each need
bespoke handling under the boolean. With separate enum values, each
orientation lowers independently.

Swapped enums are the first intrinsics to exercise a non-identity ACC
swizzle permutation: `Codegen::expand` on intrinsics_n then intrinsics_m
interleaves N and M dims in memory. Two prerequisite commits make that
permutation observable consistently across the type and encoder sides:

- #24437 makes `DataTiledMMAAttr::getUndistributedTileTypes` honor the
swizzle's permutation (rank-N tile type that reflects the actual memory
order).
- The predecessor commit on this branch attaches the swizzle to the
encoder's `MaterializeEncodingInfo` (`info.swizzle = ...`) so the packed
inner tile is the swizzle's permuted-expanded layout — the encoder-side
counterpart to #24437.

With both in place, the `reshapeToSwizzleDistributed` bridge in
`MMAUtils.cpp` collapses to a plain `vector.shape_cast` — same as it was
before non-identity permutations existed. New CHECKs in
`lower_inner_tiled.mlir`'s `lower_avx512_16x1x1_f32` pin the shape_cast
pair on the first multi-non-unit-dim swapped-intrinsic test case in the
file.

RDNA4 regression delta from #24404: the reverted PR left
`getUndistributedTileTypes` returning the wrong shape and introduced an
explicit `vector.transpose` in `reshapeToSwizzleDistributed` to
compensate. That transpose was correct for CPU but on GPU stacked on top
of GPU's already-permuted distributed shape, scrambling per-lane data on
RDNA4 (the only target whose swizzle had a non-trivial permutation at
the time). Fixing the tile type at the source removes the transpose and
keeps the shared lowering body uniform across targets.

Progress towards #24323.

Signed-off-by: Benoit Jacob <jacob.benoit.1@gmail.com>
name: llama_8b_fp16/decode_benchmark_seq128_mi325.json

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Lower explicit workgroup-local allocs through dispatch ABI (#24279)

Add #iree_codegen.workgroup_local as a codegen memory-space attribute
for authored LLVMCPU dispatch allocations that should use HAL workgroup
local memory instead of the thread stack.

This deliberately matches the GPU-side semantic split: workgroup/shared
memory is represented as memref.alloc in a workgroup memory space, while
memref.alloca remains private stack scratch. LLVMCPU uses an
IREE-specific memory-space attribute instead of
#gpu.address_space<workgroup>, but keeps the same alloc/dealloc
ownership model.

The assignment pass is intentionally narrow: it only handles entry-block
memref.alloc operations in HAL executable exports, computes byte ranges
with the target data layout and ABI alignment, rejects dynamic or
unsupported layouts, and refuses to overwrite existing local-memory
assignments or predeclared export requirements.

ConvertToLLVM consumes the assigned range by building memref descriptors
from the HAL workgroup local-memory pointer. Matching memref.dealloc
operations are erased because the storage is owned by the dispatch
frame.
